questions.q: Which key combination jumps to cell A1?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+Home goes to A1**; Ctrl+End jumps to the last used cell.

questions.q: Digital computers represent all data using —
questions.solution: A **digital** computer converts every input into **discrete binary values (0 and 1)** and computes on them. Continuous quantities are the domain of analog machines.

questions.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+J applies which alignment to the selected paragraph?
questions.solution: Ctrl+J justifies text so both margins are straight. Left is Ctrl+L, centre is Ctrl+E and right is Ctrl+R.

questions.q: Which statement about **analog computers** is correct?
options: They work on discrete binary digits
They are faster than all digital supercomputers
They were invented in the fourth generation
questions.solution: Analog computers **measure** continuous quantities — temperature, pressure, voltage, speed — and work directly on those signals. They predate digital machines and are not used for general computing today.
questions.shortcut: Analog = 'a needle that slides', not digits.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Entrepreneur** = entre + pre + neur, from French. The ending is **-eur** (like connoisseur), and there is an r after the second p.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The patient said to the doctor, "Please prescribe a milder tablet."
options: The patient requested the doctor prescribing a milder tablet.
The patient requested the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.
The patient requested to the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.
The patient ordered the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.
questions.solution: Please → **requested the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.** The listener follows requested directly; the verb after to stays bare. 'Requested the doctor prescribing' swaps the frame; 'requested to the doctor' inserts an impossible to; 'ordered the doctor' has a patient commanding a doctor — the tone is absurd.
questions.shortcut: please → requested + object + to + V1. Never 'to the doctor'.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Once in a blue moon
questions.solution: A blue moon (a second full moon in a month) hardly ever occurs → **very rarely**. 'Every month' and 'on a full-moon night' are literal moon options — photographable decoys.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The new trainee ___ several mistakes in his first report but corrected them quickly.
questions.solution: Mistakes are **made** (or committed). 'Did mistakes' is the commonest Indian-English slip; 'took' and 'gave' do not partner mistake at all.
questions.shortcut: make a mistake, never do a mistake.

questions.q: During the monsoon months the western side of the Western Ghats is wet, while the interior Deccan is comparatively dry. This is mainly due to:
questions.solution: Moist winds are forced up by the mountains (**orographic rainfall**) and shed rain on the windward side; the leeward side stays dry. Cherrapunji's rain is also orographic.

questions.q: Day and night on the Earth are caused by:
questions.solution: The Earth's **rotation** on its axis once in about 24 hours turns one half towards the Sun (day) and the other away (night). Revolution causes the seasons.

questions.q: The **Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)** is located at —
questions.solution: **FTII (1960)** — on the former Prabhat Studio campus in Pune.

questions.q: The **chlor-alkali process** (electrolysis of brine) produces —
options: Washing soda and bleaching powder only
questions.solution: Electrolysing concentrated brine gives **caustic soda at the cathode, chlorine at the anode and hydrogen** — the 'chlor-alkali' trio.

questions.q: After two equal successive discounts, an article marked at ₹6,400 is sold for ₹5,184. Each discount is:
questions.solution: Kept fraction $= \frac{5184}{6400} = 0.81 = 0.9^2$ → each discount $= 10\%$.
questions.shortcut: 9.5% halves the total 19% — successive discounts do not split evenly.

questions.q: The present average age of A, B and C is 30 years. Four years ago, the average age of B and C was 24 years. What will be A's age 4 years from now?
questions.solution: A + B + C $= 90$ now. B + C now $= 48 + 8 = 56$. So A $= 34$ now → 4 years hence $= 38$.
questions.shortcut: 46 forgets to age B and C by 4 years each.

questions.q: If $\frac{x+y}{x-y} = \frac{5}{3}$, then $\frac{x}{y}$ equals:
questions.solution: By componendo and dividendo: $\frac{x}{y} = \frac{5+3}{5-3} = \frac{8}{2} = 4$.

questions.q: From 50 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 4:1, 10 litres are removed and replaced with pure milk. The new ratio of milk to water is:
questions.solution: Draw removes 8 milk, 2 water → 32, 8; add 10 milk → $42:8 = 21:4$.
questions.shortcut: Here the milk column *grows* — the replacement is milk, not water.

questions.q: Find the value of **60 − 12 + 8 − 6**.
questions.solution: + and − have the same rank: 60 − 12 = 48, 48 + 8 = 56, 56 − 6 = **50**. Adding 12 + 8 first (60 − 20 − 6 = 34) is the trap.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**169, 196, 225, 250**
questions.solution: 169 = 13², 196 = 14², 225 = 15² are **perfect squares**. 250 lies between 15² = 225 and 16² = 256 → **250**.
questions.shortcut: A square never ends in a single 0 - 250 is out at a glance.

questions.q: A cube is painted on all its faces and cut into identical small cubes. Exactly **36** small cubes have exactly two painted faces. How many small cubes have exactly **one** painted face?
questions.solution: 12(n − 2) = 36 gives n − 2 = 3, so n = 5. Then one-face cubes = 6(n − 2)² = 6 × 3² = 6 × 0 = **54**.
questions.shortcut: Divide by 12 to get n − 2, then use 6(n − 2)².
